title: Compose the configured Telegram webhook runtime

shared_paths_approval.reason: Accepted deployable composition of the already reviewed injected Telegram transport, using only optional environment configuration and synthetic tests.

requirements: Add optional Telegram runtime settings for enabled flag, integration id, webhook secret, bot token, channel HMAC secret and digest key version. Disabled is the default. Enabled configuration is all-or-nothing, strictly validated, and errors mention only setting names/codes, never values. Secrets remain absent from repr and public responses.

Add a composition factory that builds exactly the reviewed chain TelegramUpdateAdapter → ChannelIdentityService → PostgresChannelDraftPort/ChannelGateway/ChannelConversation → Telegram mapper/resolvers/orchestrator/renderer → TelegramBotApiClient/WebhookRuntime from supplied settings, Engine and optional injected httpx AsyncClient. No business rules are duplicated.

When create_app receives no explicit telegram_webhook_runtime and Telegram is enabled, compose it with the configured database and one owned HTTP client. Explicit injection remains authoritative for tests. When disabled the endpoint keeps the current 503 behavior. Close only resources owned by the app during shutdown; never close injected client/engine resources.

Extend .env.example only with blank/synthetic-safe Telegram variable names and comments; no usable token, webhook secret or HMAC secret is committed. Production startup with partial/invalid enabled configuration fails closed before serving requests.

Add tests for disabled, complete, partial, invalid, secret-safe repr/error behavior, explicit-injection precedence, owned-resource shutdown and a disposable PostgreSQL composition smoke through the real webhook route with MockTransport. No live Telegram request or real credential is used.

Do not call setWebhook, add webhook registration, polling, retries/background workers, VK, owner notifications, migrations, deployment, frontend or documentation. Commit this exact task specification at tasks/specs/TG-017.json.
acceptance: A locally configured application can serve the reviewed Telegram webhook without manually constructing runtime objects in application code.
Disabled and invalid configurations fail safely, secrets do not appear in representations/errors, and application-owned resources close exactly once.
Focused composition/settings/API, Telegram regression, full pytest and whitespace gates pass within allowed scope.
